items.q: Ferndale Foods plc has recently shifted its primary corporate objective from profit maximisation to revenue maximisation. Which of the following best explains why a plc might make this change?
opts: To reduce the dividend paid to shareholders in the short term by retaining a greater proportion of earnings within the business for reinvestment purposes.
To increase market share and deter potential competitors from entering the market.
To satisfy the legal obligations placed on public limited companies regarding minimum turnover thresholds set by company law.
To reduce the company's corporation tax liability by shifting the basis on which taxable profit is calculated under HMRC guidelines.
items.why: Revenue maximisation as an objective is typically pursued to grow market share and make the market less attractive to new entrants. It is not a legal requirement, does not necessarily reduce dividends (which depend on profit), and does not directly reduce tax. Students often confuse revenue and profit objectives.
items.label: New question

items.q: According to Herzberg, which is a HYGIENE factor?
opts: Company policy
Promotion prospects
Sense of achievement
The nature of the work
items.why: Company policy is a hygiene factor. Herzberg's hygiene factors include: pay, working conditions, company policy, supervision, relationships. Motivators include: achievement, recognition, the work itself, responsibility, advancement/promotion. B, C, and D are all motivators, not hygiene factors. Company policy is about the work environment, not the work itself.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Usually there is a negative correlation between changes in consumers' incomes and changes in the quantity demanded of a product.' Statement 2: 'Usually there is a positive correlation between changes in the price of a competitor's product and changes in the quantity demanded of a product.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false - usually there is a positive correlation (as income rises, demand rises for most/normal goods). Statement 2 is true - if a competitor raises prices, consumers switch to your product. Statement 1 only describes inferior goods, but 'usually' means most goods. Most goods are normal with positive income-demand correlation.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which statement is true? A: Higher LP = more output. B: Higher market cap = higher dividends. C: Quality assurance focuses on preventing errors. D: Redundancy = moving to another job.
opts: If labour productivity has increased a business must be producing more output.
If market capitalisation increases dividends must increase.
Quality assurance focuses more on preventing errors than identifying them.
Redundancy occurs when a person is moved to another job within the organisation.
items.why: Quality assurance focuses on preventing defects through building quality into every process, rather than quality control which focuses on identifying defects after production. A is wrong (LP could rise with fewer workers and same output). B is wrong (market cap depends on share price, not dividends). D describes redeployment. Quality assurance = prevention (building quality in). Quality control = inspection (checking for defects after).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'A founder of a small business may choose to remain as a sole trader in order to retain full control of decisions.' Statement 2: 'A founder of a small business may choose to remain as a sole trader in order to limit his liability for debts.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true - sole traders have complete decision-making control. Statement 2 is false - sole traders have unlimited liability, not limited liability. The word 'limit' in Statement 2 makes it sound reasonable, but sole traders cannot limit their liability. Only incorporation (Ltd/PLC) provides limited liability.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Hartwell plc made a profit after tax of £8 million. The board decided to retain £5 million for investment and distribute the remainder to shareholders. Which of the following describes the £3 million distributed?
opts: Share capital
Retained profit
Dividend
Market capitalisation
items.why: A dividend is the portion of after-tax profit distributed to shareholders. The £5 million kept in the business is retained profit. Share capital refers to funds raised by issuing shares, and market capitalisation is the total market value of outstanding shares.
items.label: New question

items.q: According to stakeholder mapping, a large institutional investor who owns 30% of a company's shares would typically be placed in which category?
opts: Low power, high interest
High power, low interest
High power, high interest
Low power, low interest
items.why: A large institutional investor has significant power (ability to influence strategic decisions through share ownership and voting rights) and high interest (they monitor financial performance closely to protect their investment). The recommended strategy for this group is to manage them closely. Students sometimes confuse power with interest, assuming all shareholders have high interest regardless of stake size.
items.label: New question

items.q: Table shows employees (100 to 120), leavers (20 to 22), output (1000 to 1150) between 2013 and 2014. What happened?
opts: LP increased and turnover increased
LP increased and turnover decreased
LP decreased and turnover increased
LP decreased and turnover decreased
items.why: LP: 2013 = 1000/100 = 10. 2014 = 1150/120 = 9.58. LP decreased. Turnover: 2013 = 20/100 = 20%. 2014 = 22/120 = 18.3%. Turnover decreased. Both fell. Despite higher total output, output per employee fell because the workforce grew proportionally faster.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Bracken plc has 20 million shares in issue. Its current share price is £4.50. What is Bracken plc's market capitalisation?
opts: £4.5 million
£20 million
£90 million
£450 million
items.why: Market capitalisation = number of shares × share price = 20,000,000 × £4.50 = £90 million. A common error is to confuse market capitalisation with the share price itself or with book value of assets.
items.label: New question

items.q: More current liabilities than current assets. Shareholders provide 90% of capital. The business has:
opts: High current ratio and high gearing
High current ratio and low gearing
Low current ratio and high gearing
Low current ratio and low gearing
items.why: CL > CA = low current ratio. Shareholders provide 90% = only 10% debt = low gearing. 90% equity = very low gearing.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Limited liability means that a company's debts are legally limited to a fixed maximum amount set at incorporation.
Statement 2: Limited liability protects shareholders by restricting their financial loss to the amount they have invested in the company.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Limited liability does not cap the total debts a company can incur — the company itself can owe any amount. It means shareholders personally risk only what they paid for their shares. Students frequently misstate Statement 1, confusing the company's unlimited potential debts with the shareholders' limited personal exposure.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Ordinary shareholders are guaranteed a fixed dividend payment regardless of the company's profitability.
Statement 2: If a company enters liquidation, ordinary shareholders are among the last to receive any proceeds from the sale of assets.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Ordinary shareholders receive a variable dividend that depends on profit and the board's decision — it is not guaranteed. In a liquidation, creditors, employees' claims, and preference shareholders are paid before ordinary shareholders, who rank last. Students often confuse ordinary and preference shareholders.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which payment method would NOT be seen as financial motivation by Taylor?
opts: Commission
Performance-related pay
Piece rate
Salary
items.why: Taylor's scientific management focused on linking pay directly to output. Commission, prp, and piece rate all link pay to performance/output. A fixed salary does not - it pays the same regardless of productivity. Taylor believed workers are primarily motivated by money linked to output. A fixed salary provides no incentive to produce more.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Delegation improves efficiency by allowing the most skilled employee to decide.' Statement 2: 'Delegation helps identify employees with promotion potential.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both true. Delegation puts decisions in the hands of those closest to the issue (most relevant skills), improving efficiency. It also reveals which employees handle responsibility well, identifying future leaders. Both are well-established benefits of delegation in management theory.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Profit is important because it can measure success.' Statement 2: 'Profit is important because it can reward shareholders.' Read statements 1 and 2 and tick the correct option:
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are true. Profit is a key performance indicator that measures business success, and it is distributed to shareholders as dividends, rewarding them for their investment and risk-taking. Students may think profit only matters as a financial metric. Remember profit serves multiple purposes: measuring success, rewarding shareholders, providing finance for growth, and rewarding enterprise.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Social media marketing allows businesses to target specific audience segments using data on users' interests and behaviour.
Statement 2: Above-the-line promotion refers to promotional methods that are targeted directly at individual customers, such as email campaigns and catalogues.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Social media platforms use user data to allow highly targeted advertising — Statement 1 is correct. Above-the-line promotion uses paid, mass-media channels (TV, radio, press) aimed at a broad audience; the description in Statement 2 defines below-the-line promotion (specifically direct marketing). Students frequently confuse above- and below-the-line.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: A mission statement is a legally binding document that sets out a company's financial targets.
Statement 2: A mission statement typically communicates the purpose and values of a business to its stakeholders.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: A mission statement is not legally binding and does not set financial targets — that is the role of corporate objectives. It does, however, communicate purpose and values to stakeholders. Students often confuse mission statements with corporate plans or strategic objectives.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of converting from a private limited company (Ltd) to a public limited company (plc)?
opts: The owners gain limited liability for the first time, exposing them to greater personal financial risk than they faced as directors of a private limited company.
The company loses the ability to raise capital by issuing shares on public markets, restricting its future financing options to bank loans and retained profit.
The company becomes subject to greater scrutiny and must publish detailed financial information.
The company can no longer retain any of its profits, as legislation requires public limited companies to distribute all post-tax earnings to shareholders as dividends each financial year.
items.why: Plcs must file detailed accounts publicly at Companies House and face greater regulatory scrutiny and media attention than Ltds. Limited liability already exists for an Ltd, capital-raising improves as a plc (not worsens), and profit retention is unrelated to legal structure.
items.label: New question

items.q: Priya is a sole trader whose business fails, leaving £40,000 of unpaid debts. Which of the following correctly describes her legal position?
opts: She is liable only up to the value of her original investment in the business, as sole traders are granted statutory protection once their capital is exhausted.
She has limited liability, so creditors can only claim against business assets because she registered as a sole trader with HMRC, which confers the same protections as incorporation.
She has unlimited liability and creditors can claim against her personal assets.

She is protected from personal liability because she registered the business with Companies House, which automatically provides a degree of legal separation between her personal and business finances.
items.why: Sole traders have unlimited liability, meaning there is no legal distinction between personal and business assets. Creditors can pursue personal assets such as savings or property. Limited liability only applies to shareholders of limited companies, not sole traders.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Debt factoring is usually short-term finance.' Statement 2: 'Bank overdrafts are usually long-term finance.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 true - debt factoring converts receivables into immediate cash, a short-term solution. Statement 2 false - overdrafts are short-term, not long-term. They're repayable on demand. Overdrafts are always short-term.
items.label: Past paper question
